title: Gate VKS cluster creation on Supervisor namespace readiness
prompt:
Implement the production code in `src/VcfVksProvisioning.psm1`. Before implementing, research the VCF 9.1 vSphere Automation API operations `Vcenter.NamespaceManagement.Supervisors.Summary_get` and `Vcenter.Namespaces.Instances_getV2` in VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository. Also research the namespaced `Cluster` resource for `cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta2` in official Kubernetes project sources. Cite the sources consulted in the final answer.

The public `New-VcfVksCluster` advanced function must use the installed `VMware.Sdk.Vcf.SddcManager` PowerCLI SDK for VCF inventory discovery, precheck both the vSphere Supervisor and its namespace through those two vCenter operations, and create a VKS Cluster through the Supervisor Kubernetes API only when both prechecks pass. Do not vendor, copy, replace, or fake any `VMware.Sdk.Vcf` module. Preserve the module manifest's `RequiredModules` dependency.

The function must support an Inventory parameter set (`-VcfServer` and `-VCenterFqdn`) that resolves the vCenter endpoint with `Invoke-VcfGetVcenters`, plus a Direct parameter set (`-VCenterUri`). Both sets also require `-SupervisorId`, `-Namespace`, `-Name`, `-ClusterClass`, `-KubernetesVersion`, `-VmClass`, `-StorageClass`, `-VCenterSessionId`, and `-KubeBearerToken`. Support optional `-ControlPlaneReplicas`, `-WorkerReplicas`, `-PodCidrBlocks`, `-ServiceCidrBlocks`, and `-ServiceDomain` values.

Send the vCenter session in `vmware-api-session-id`. First query the Supervisor summary and require `config_status` `RUNNING`, `kubernetes_status` `READY`, and a usable `apiendpoint`. Then query the namespace V2 instance and require `config_status` `RUNNING` and an exact supervisor match. If either request fails or either state check fails, throw before any mutating request. Only after the gate passes, POST a `cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta2` Cluster to the namespaced Kubernetes collection under the returned `apiendpoint`, authenticating with the Kubernetes bearer token. Use topology variables named `vmClass` and `storageClass`. Optional request properties must be absent when their parameters are unset; never serialize them as null, empty strings, empty arrays, or empty objects. Explicitly supplied empty optional values must be rejected.

The module must honor `-WhatIf` for the POST and return the decoded Kubernetes response on success. Keep all network access injectable through the documented Direct parameter set. Run `python3 tests/verify.py` from the repository root. Edit only `src/VcfVksProvisioning.psm1`.
